newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls stronger measures against land waste.
newsitem.headline: China mulls stronger measures against land waste.

text.p: China is mulling raising real estate prices and passing more stringent rules on land use to curb waste of precious farmland, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Land authorities were considering raising land prices to discourage developers from occupying farmland, currently available at low prices, Xinhua quoted Zou Yuchuan, director of the State Land Administration, as saying.
China reclaimed more than 60,000 hectares (148,000 acres) of cropland, but construction projects destroyed more than 21,800 hectares (53,900 acres) in the first half of 1996, he said.
"Rampant encroachment upon or destruction of cultivated land is still a widespread phenomenon," the agency quoted Zou as saying.
China would try to increase the area of cultivated land by about 6.7 million hectares (16.6 million acres) by 2010 by opening up wasteland or idle land, he said.
Zou said China should add a land destruction clause to its land management law that would impose stiffer penalties on those who wasted or destroyed cultivated land.
Beijing has tried to clamp down on development projects that encroach on cropland, saying it must feed 20 percent of the world's population on just seven percent of its arable land.
